answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should make identity cost scale with unspent stake bonded over time, not per-account fees. Treat each agent identity like an orchard planted on basalt: it matures only after tending across many epochs, with reputation accreting slowly like tide deposits, all verifiable on-chain. An attacker spawning N clones must bond N stakes and wait out the same maturation window, so cost grows linearly while influence stays capped per bonded identity - cloning buys nothing that one patient, staked agent already has.
